query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small interstitial addition of boron into the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy will improve its ductility and toughness by modifying the grain boundary characteristics and reducing crack nucleation sites.
generation.material_initial_state: HfZrTi high-entropy alloy in its standard as-cast or annealed condition without interstitial boron.
generation.intervention: Incorporate a minor amount (on the order of a few atomic percent, e.g., ~2 at%) of boron into the alloy composition during synthesis.
generation.conditions: Samples processed under controlled melting and casting conditions, followed by homogenization heat treatment, ensuring uniform distribution of boron; mechanical testing performed at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron is expected to segregate preferentially to grain boundaries or form fine boride precipitates at the interfaces, thereby modifying the boundary cohesion and overall microstructural stability.
generation.mechanism: The presence of boron at grain boundaries is hypothesized to reduce the tendency for intergranular cracking by enhancing grain boundary cohesion and possibly promoting more uniform plastic deformation. Additionally, if nanoscale boride precipitates form, they could help deflect or blunt propagating cracks, contributing to increased toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in measured ductility (e.g., higher elongation to fracture) and toughness (e.g., higher fracture toughness values) compared to the boron-free alloy, without a deleterious reduction in strength.
generation.baseline: Mechanical properties (tensile strength, ductility, fracture toughness) of the unmodified HfZrTi high-entropy alloy.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are hypothesized for a narrow compositional window of boron addition; beyond this, excessive boron could lead to the formation of brittle phases. Effects may also depend sensitively on the heat treatment and processing conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Direct evidence for boron’s effect on the HfZrTi HEA system is currently limited, making the exact optimal boron concentration and mechanism (i.e., segregation versus precipitation) uncertain. The hypothesis relies on analogy with other alloy systems where interstitial boron has improved mechanical properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of HfZrTi high-entropy alloy samples: one with a controlled addition of ~2 at% boron and one set without boron. Process both sets under identical melting, homogenization, and annealing conditions. Conduct standardized tensile tests and fracture toughness measurements at room temperature, supplemented by microstructural analysis (e.g., SEM/TEM) to study grain boundary chemistry and precipitate formation.
measurements: Tensile strength and elongation to fracture
Microstructural characterization (grain size, presence of boride phases, grain boundary chemistry via EDS or atom probe tomography)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-containing samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in ductility and fracture toughness over the baseline (within experimental error) or if the addition results in the formation of brittle phases that degrade mechanical properties, then the hypothesis is falsified.
